headline: HG deal lifts output, but softer gas prices hit profit
summary_short: Revenue rose 20% y/y to $1.56 billion but fell 20% q/q as softer natural gas prices offset a 21% y/y jump in production from the HG Acquisition. Diluted EPS was $0.90, down from $1.72 in Q1 but up from $0.50 a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue was $1.56B (+20.2% y/y, -19.8% q/q) as the HG Acquisition lifted daily combined production 21% y/y to 4,144 MMcfe/d, but a 22% y/y drop in the average unhedged natural gas price ($2.66/Mcf) offset most of the volume gain; the hedged realized gas price fell a smaller 5% to $3.18/Mcf. Diluted EPS was $0.90 (-47.7% q/q, +80.0% y/y). Operating income was $375M (-48.5% q/q, +83.3% y/y) as Q2's commodity-derivative gain of $161M outpaced Q2 2025's $53M. Long-term debt rose to $2.43B from $1.10B y/y funding the HG deal, partly offset by $757M of Utica Shale Divestiture proceeds. FY2026 capital budget stands at $1.1-1.3B, unchanged from the February announcement.

drivers.explanation: Q2 reflects the post-HG-Acquisition production step-up colliding with softer natural gas prices; the filing also notes the Utica Shale Divestiture (closed Feb 23, 2026) and a Credit Facility maturity extension to July 2031 as concurrent portfolio and liquidity moves.

HG Acquisition properties added $143M of Q2 gas revenue and lifted volumes; higher natural gas production added roughly $190M y/y, but a lower average price cut roughly $189M, largely offsetting the volume gain.
Higher combined production (+21% y/y) and $161M of commodity-derivative fair value gains (vs $53M in Q2 2025) drove the y/y improvement, partly offset by lower per-unit realized prices.
Increase reflects borrowings under the Term Loan and issuance of the 2036 Notes to fund the $2.8B HG Acquisition, which closed February 3, 2026.
